# Independent QPACK vectors

These eight files extract ordered request fields, raw field-section bytes and
the complete encoder instruction sequence from Surf's original real Chromium
156.0.8078.79 / Firefox 159.0.1 captures. Each file pins its source URL and SHA-256.
Expected bytes are copied from those captures, never generated by this encoder.
The original captures and their provenance remain in Surf's `browser_sequences`.

Generic encoder options are fixture inputs. There are no browser modes in the
runtime encoder. `settings_before_request` fixes the SETTINGS event position from
the initial observed compression state; subsequent section acknowledgments model
the captured peer's sequential decode/response progression. Peer capacities are
0, 128, 4096 and 65536. Each sequence contains eleven requests with repeated and
changed fields, credentials and cookies on one connection.

`TestEncoderIndependentBrowserVectors` checks all 88 complete field sections and
all eight encoder instruction streams byte for byte. This isolates compression
from network scheduling: a real first request can arrive before SETTINGS and
remain static, leading to a different valid table history. It does not establish
equal QUIC packet timing or require waiting for SETTINGS before sending a request.
